title: Drain and sum
hints: There is a loop form made for exactly this: it receives one value per iteration and ends by itself once the channel is closed and empty.

`for v := range ch { … }` waits for each value, so it also handles a sender that is still working. Don't use `len(ch)` to decide when to stop, and don't loop on a plain `v := <-ch`: after close it returns zero values forever.
`Sum`: `total := 0; for v := range ch { total += v }; return total`. `Drain`: `var out []T; for v := range ch { out = append(out, v) }; return out`.
